title: A combination of non-standard exit behavior (eg. Ctrl+Z) plus no conversation history creates a poor user experience
body:
> This non-conventional use of Ctrl+Z to exit out of ClaudeCode is driving me up the wall. I can't be the only one.

● I understand your frustration with the Ctrl+Z behavior in Claude Code. This is indeed a common complaint from
  users who expect more conventional exit shortcuts.

● Fetch(https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/interactive-mode)
  ⎿  No (tell Claude what to do differently)

> It wouldn't be so bad if conversations were stored, like they are in the Claude.ai web browser experience.

● You're absolutely right - the lack of conversation persistence makes the Ctrl+Z exit behavior much more
  frustrating. In the web interface, you can easily return to previous conversations, but in Claude Code, once you
  exit, that context is gone.

  This combination of non-standard exit behavior + no conversation history creates a poor user experience,
  especially when you're in the middle of working through complex tasks or debugging sessions.

  You might want to consider providing feedback about this at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues -
  the combination of these two UX issues seems like something the team should address.
author: iamthefaker
